precepts.text: Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble; thou wilt prepare their heart. Humble yourself to whatever the Bible says.
precepts.point: Ezra had prepared his heart, his mind, to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. We are in captivity, working and tired, and the Most High reminds us these are the last days, so prepare your mind.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
“For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” What is the heart? The mind. Ezra had prepared his mind to seek the Lord his God. We are in captivity, always working and tired; some days you get stressed. But the Most High has to remind us that we are living in the last days. So brothers, prepare your minds; sisters, prepare your minds.

David shows who the Lord prepares: “Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear”. We are the humble. We are supposed to humble ourselves to whatever the Bible says we ought to do.

And when we humble ourselves, the Lord hears our desire and prepares our hearts. We will prepare our minds. That is what Ezra did before he went to teach Israel, and that is what is required of us now, as we watch Iran and Israel go to war and America get involved, and more of our people wake up and repent.

precepts.text: They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts and humble their souls in his sight. War is imminent and the birthing pains will get worse; prepare your mind so that whatever evil comes you remain faithful, and rejoice, because the scriptures said it would happen.
precepts.point: Ezra had prepared his heart, his mind, to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. We are in captivity, working and tired, and the Most High reminds us these are the last days, so prepare your mind.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Why prepare our minds and our spirits? Because war is imminent. We are seeing Iran and Israel at war and America getting involved, and the wars are only going to get worse. What we see right now is a birthing pain. Yet all of us are supposed to rejoice, because the scriptures already told us this was going to happen.

Sirach says: “They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight”. All of us that fear the Lord will prepare our minds, so that whatever evil comes upon the earth, we will remain faithful in serving the Lord.

That is Ezra's example: a heart prepared, and a soul humbled in the Lord's sight, ready to seek the law, do it, and teach it, whatever comes.

precepts.text: A man of understanding trusteth in the law, and the law is faithful unto him. Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard: in prayer, in the streets, in leading and organizing blacks and Hispanics. Bind up instruction, and then make answer.
precepts.point: Ezra had prepared his heart, his mind, to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. We are in captivity, working and tired, and the Most High reminds us these are the last days, so prepare your mind.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law and to teach it. Sirach shows why: “A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him, as an oracle.” We must trust in the laws of God, and the law will be faithful unto us.

“Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard”. We have to prepare what to say. Prepare what to say in prayer when we speak to the Most High, and we will be heard. Prepare what to say and teach in the streets, and we will be heard. We must prepare to lead, guide and organize blacks and Hispanics.

“and bind up instruction, and then make answer.” Bind up the instruction first, and then make answer. That is how Ezra could teach in Israel statutes and judgments: he had prepared his heart before he opened his mouth.

precepts.text: Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; hear the word at my mouth and give them warning from me. To the teachers and the brothers in the MOV program: not the Bishop, the deacons, or the captains made you a watchman. The Lord called you to warn Israel to repent.
precepts.point: Ezra had prepared his heart, his mind, to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. We are in captivity, working and tired, and the Most High reminds us these are the last days, so prepare your mind.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
This is to the brothers who teach, the up-and-coming soldiers in the MOV program. Ezra prepared his heart to teach in Israel, and the Lord says: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

Who is speaking? The Most High said, I have made thee a watchman. It is not the Bishop that made you a watchman. It is not the deacons, and it is not the captains. The Lord called you to be a watchman. That is why you were called into this truth: to warn our people, to warn Israel that they need to repent.

Habakkuk shows the watchman's posture: “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. He is awake and paying attention. As watchmen we must be faithful and pay attention to the signs of the times, hear the word at the Lord's mouth, and give Israel warning from him.

precepts.text: Preparing the heart is setting the house in order and casting off mortal thoughts and the weak nature.
precepts.point: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

precepts.why:
“Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” What preparing the heart means is shown to Ezra himself: “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption, Let go from thee mortal thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature.”

To prepare the heart is to set the mind and spirit in order, to examine yourself, to renounce corruption and let go of mortal thoughts, and to put off the weak nature of sin. Ezra did that before he taught statutes and judgments in Israel: he set his own house in order first, and then reproved and comforted the people.

precepts.text: Ezra's great skill in the word came because he prayed and fasted to understand, and the Most High did great works through him.
precepts.point: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

precepts.why:
The fruit of Ezra's prepared heart is told in 1 Esdras: “Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.”

That great skill in the word came because he prayed and fasted to understand, and the Most High did great works through him. He came to Jerusalem “according to the good hand of his God upon him”, and having sought the law and done it, he taught all Israel, omitting nothing of the law and commandments.

precepts.text: Whoever lacks wisdom may ask of God, who gives to all men liberally, and it shall be given.
precepts.point: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

precepts.why:
Ezra's skill in the law was not his own. “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.”

Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law, and the understanding to teach statutes and judgments in Israel was given him by the good hand of his God. Whoever lacks wisdom today may do the same: ask of God, who gives to all men liberally and does not upbraid, and it shall be given.

precepts.text: The abundance of the nations and their wealth shall be brought and turned unto restored Israel.
precepts.point: The king and his counselors freely offered silver and gold for the house of God, for sacrifices, and for whatever else was needful, drawn even from the king's treasure house. This was favor, letting the captivity return with the treasures of Babylon, as the nations will one day bring back all Israel's substance.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

precepts.why:
Artaxerxes and his counsellors freely offered silver and gold “unto the God of Israel, whose habitation is in Jerusalem”, and told Ezra to carry all the silver and gold he could find in the province of Babylon, and to bestow whatever more was needful “out of the king’s treasure house.” That was favor: the captivity going home with the treasures of Babylon.

It is a picture of what the nations will one day do for all Israel. “Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee. The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the Lord.”

The abundance of the nations and their wealth shall be brought and turned unto restored Israel. Ezra carrying the king's silver and gold up to Jerusalem is a foretaste of the nations bringing back all of Israel's substance.
